chunks: Al-Kafi: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fadhal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'as ruled by two just men among you'
He said: The just man is the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and the Imam after him
Then he said: This is among that which the scribes made a mistake in.

key_terms.أَخْطَأَتْ بِهِ الْكِتَابُ: the scribes made a mistake in it

ai.seo_question: Who is the 'just man' referred to in the Quranic verse according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Zurara queries Imam al-Baqir regarding the Quranic phrase 'two just men' (ذَوَا عَدْلٍ), to which the Imam identifies the 'just man' as the Messenger of Allah and the subsequent Imam, indicating their infallible authority. He concludes that this interpretation is what the scribes may have erred in recording or understanding in the written text. This hadith highlights the Shia belief in the divine appointment of Imams as the ultimate interpreters of Quranic justice.

en.ammaar-muslim: 2. [2/89] al-Kafi: Muhammad b. Yahya from Ahmad b. Muhammad from Ibn Fadhal from Ibn Bukayr from Zurara who said:
I asked Aba Ja’far عليه السلام about the words of Allah Mighty and Majestic: “as ruled by two just men among you” [5:95]
– he said: the just man is the messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and the Imam after him,
then he said: this is among that which the scribes made a mistake in.
